title: Bill Gates first called for robot taxes in 2017, nine years later, he again raises 'Tax the robots' sloga
key_facts: Gates said last week, to Ezra Klein of The New York Times, that AI should pay taxes to compensate for destroyed jobs.
He asked why a robot replacing a worker should not pay into the pension fund.
About half a dozen US proposals to tax AI labs have been introduced and made little headway.
Reps. Casar, Foushee and Jacobs proposed an AI tax to fund an employment programme.
Sen. Sanders proposed a share-based levy on AI companies with at least $200 million in AI revenue.
Sen. Warren and Sen. Kelly have also proposed AI-related taxes.
Think tanks urge caution because AI's effects on work are still unknown.
quote_evidence: "If you've let go of a worker and hired a robot to do that job, why are you so incentivizing the trade-off against the human labor that you don't ask the robot to also pay into the pension fund?" the tech guru said last week in an interview with Ezra Klein in The New York Times.
The proposals have made little headway so far because Democrats do not control either chamber of Congress, but with midterm elections around the corner, the balance of power could change.
why_it_matters_hint: Gates's remark revives a growing US debate on taxing AI to protect pensions.
event_date: late Sep or early Oct 2026 (NYT interview, 'last week')
